input.rationale: The multi-voter variant that question-0 listed as unwitnessed is now built and probed. A three-voter cluster takes one deliberate snapshot (automatic snapshots disabled so nothing newer can cover the change), grows to five voters, and the leader is restarted from its own stores: with RestoreCommittedLogs on it comes back holding the snapshot's three-voter configuration at index 1 while its own log's latest configuration is index 14 with five servers; without the flag the same restart keeps index 14 with five servers. That addresses the single-voter limitation with a real membership change, not just a bootstrap entry. A second consequence was attempted in the same harness: after restarting, the node is partitioned together with one committed voter so that the remaining three voters hold a majority of the committed five-voter configuration while the restarted node believes the quorum is two. In the probe the restarted node did not campaign to leadership (became_leader false in both modes) although the majority side did keep a leader, so that consequence is recorded as an attempted discrimination that did not emerge rather than as a claim; only the configuration comparison is declared. Nothing else is restated.

investigations.question: Does the configuration loss also occur for a real membership change in a multi-voter cluster, and can the resulting stale membership produce a decision the committed configuration would not allow?
investigations.hypothesis: A node restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs keeps the snapshot's configuration when committed membership changes sit below the restored commit index, so its quorum arithmetic reflects an obsolete membership.
investigations.discriminator: Grow a snapshot-age three-voter cluster to five voters, restart the leader, and compare the configuration index and server count with the log's latest configuration; then isolate the restarted node with one committed voter and see whether it can win with its smaller quorum.

knowledge.statement: A node restarted with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs whose rebuilt configuration is empty stays a Follower and never campaigns: the latest configuration is empty, so runFollower takes the 'no known peers, aborting election' branch and quorumSize() returns one, while the same node restarted without the flag rebuilds the committed configuration and returns to Leader.

interpretations.rationale: Source: the mechanism of the parent question applies to a real membership change, not only to a bootstrap entry: restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) sets lastApplied to the persisted commit index before the scan at api.go:604-620, restoreSnapshot (api.go:655-681) can only supply the snapshot's configuration, and AddVoter (api.go:994-1005) writes a later LogConfiguration that is re-read only if it sits above the restored commit index. A native construction probe reproduced the predicted difference with five committed voters: with the flag on the restarted leader came back with after_latest_index 1 and after_servers 3 (the snapshot's bootstrap configuration) against expected_latest_index 14 and expected_servers 5, while the flag-off control came back with index 14 and five servers; the pre-restart state was index 14 with five servers in both modes, so the change itself committed in both. A second consequence was attempted and did not emerge: after the restart the node was partitioned together with one committed voter while the remaining three voters kept a majority of the committed five-voter configuration, and the restarted node never reached Leader in either mode (became_leader false, majority_side_leader true, reachable_votes 2 against committed_quorum 3), so an election won with a minority of the committed configuration is not claimed. Only the configuration comparison is declared, and only its receipt can make it complete.
counterevidence: The flag-off control keeps the five-server configuration through the same membership change and restart, isolating the flagged recovery path.

The attempted minority-election consequence did not emerge in the probe: the restarted node stayed out of leadership in both modes, so a safety consequence beyond the lost configuration remains unestablished.

interpretations.rationale: Source reading establishes the mechanism: NewRaft initialises configurations to its zero value, restoreSnapshot is the only producer that can supply a configuration from persistent state (api.go:655-681), and the only other producer is the startup log scan (api.go:610-613) starting at max(snapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1. restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) runs before that scan and calls setCommitIndex(commitIndex) then processLogs(commitIndex, nil); processLogs forwards LogConfiguration entries to the FSM (raft.go:1366-1391) and never updates r.configurations. With RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, every committed configuration entry at or below the restored commit index is therefore invisible to the node after restart. A native construction probe of a bootstrapped single node (CommitTrackingLogs, no snapshot, 10 applied entries) reproduced the predicted difference: with the flag on the event was {after_latest_index:0, after_servers:0, after_has_vote:false, after_commit_index:11, after_last_applied:11, before_latest_index:1, snapshots:0} and the library logged 'initial configuration: index=0 servers=[]'; with the flag off the same restart reported {after_latest_index:1, after_servers:1, after_has_vote:true}. The probe is construction feedback without a retained receipt, so the formal comparison is left to the submitted experiment. Consequence under the stated conditions: the restarted node's own membership view is the pre-restart snapshot value or empty, so runFollower's 'no known peers, aborting election' branch (raft.go:228-232) and the hasVote gate (raft.go:236-246) prevent it from campaigning, and quorumSize() is computed over a configuration that contradicts the committed log (raft.go:1087-1094). Counterevidence examined: a snapshot can legitimately supply the configuration (api.go:677-678) but only as of snapshot.ConfigurationIndex, which cannot cover a configuration committed after that snapshot; appendEntries processes only entries it newly appends (raft.go:1594-1621); leaderLoop only promotes latest to committed (raft.go:797-799). Limitations: the finding is scoped to the stated configuration and store conditions; the snapshot-present variant remains a registered gap; only a controller receipt can make this a completed comparison.

result.summary: Built and probed the multi-voter variant that question-0 listed as unwitnessed. A three-voter cluster takes one deliberate snapshot (automatic snapshots disabled so no newer snapshot can cover the change), grows to five voters via two added nodes, and the leading node is restarted from its own stores: with RestoreCommittedLogs on it returns holding the snapshot's bootstrap configuration at index 1 with three servers while its own log's latest configuration is index 14 with five servers, and the flag-off control keeps index 14 with five servers; the pre-restart state was index 14 with five servers in both modes, so the membership change committed in both.
